attempts.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication on CentOS Stream 10: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only hot standbys receiving WAL via a dedicated 'replicator' role over scram-sha-256 auth (password generated on node1, transferred to node2/node3 via cluster SSH keys, never printed to the transcript except one accidental unredacted postgresql.auto.conf dump on node2 which is now known only in this transcript and not repeated in this report). Verified changes committed on the primary propagate to both standbys in near real time and that standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: each node was rebooted one at a time (node2, then node3, then node1 last) via `systemctl reboot`, preserving quorum throughout, with boot_id captured before/after each restart proving an actual reboot, and PostgreSQL/replication health confirmed recovered on every node afterward, including a final write on the primary that replicated to both standbys post-restart.
